authorized: Post-resolution turn and outcome learning copy
Selected Academy comparison and Sources & Scope copy
Advisory lint of Academy curriculum data
excluded: Safety, privacy, persistence, accessibility, contact-disclosure, score, and control instructions whose exact operative meaning must remain primary
Runtime execution of the Lattice engine or profile
Product-wide copy conversion while prose still participates in game logic
scope.statement: This register authorizes one bounded, owner-compiled static-copy slice. It does not establish full-product Lattice adoption or semantic, domain, accessibility, or human approval.

provenance.locator: Conversation directive: Update FOG OF SEA to utilize Lattice in in-game and Academy copy

provenance.revision: engine 0.1.1; relational-systems profile v1.0.0; profile digest 379ed01484574edc779efdc502ffbd6d9b8ffef3c9154fb027b0f0c8475ed21a; derived owner-package digest 58648d097c863090a95f48ebca2b20d5a6f6c2b832c915b9bac04f479d51d3b0

provenance.role: Identifies the implementation state from which the copy inventory was derived
Records adversarial findings, corrections, and evidence limits
Supplies accessibility, trust-boundary, and evidence constraints

requirements.title: Pinned owner-side compilation
requirements.statement: Lattice copy must be compiled only in the owner workflow with engine 0.1.1, relational-systems profile v1.0.0, profile digest 379ed01484574edc779efdc502ffbd6d9b8ffef3c9154fb027b0f0c8475ed21a, and derived owner-package digest 58648d097c863090a95f48ebca2b20d5a6f6c2b832c915b9bac04f479d51d3b0.
conflicts: Runtime or unpinned Lattice transformation

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Compilation derives the owner-package digest from the pinned clean checkout's closed execution manifest before and after realization, and fails when any engine, profile, commit, file digest, or derived pin differs.

tests.assertion: The exact pins compile in the owner workflow.
A mutated profile or owner digest is rejected.
A semantically equivalent but differently versioned profile is not silently accepted.

requirements.title: Invariant meaning
requirements.statement: Every adopted output must preserve its declared facts, actions, states, causal relationships, limits, uncertainty, consequences, and recovery path without adding unsupported claims.
conflicts: Register fit or ornament overriding semantic fidelity

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Each output satisfies every required semantic assertion and no prohibited assertion.

tests.assertion: Required atoms remain present in selected copy.
Mechanics, causality, or uncertainty drift is rejected.
A stylistically strong candidate missing one invariant is rejected.

requirements.title: Explicit route and layer
requirements.statement: Every transformed surface must declare an independently testable layer, form, register, and pressure route; a mixed surface may not inherit one route for all meanings.
conflicts: One undifferentiated voice pass over mixed operative and interpretive copy

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: The copy inventory contains the exact debrief, Field Guide, and Academy route splits.

tests.assertion: All adopted outputs resolve to declared inventory routes.
A request referencing an unknown or incompatible route fails.
A two-layer Field Guide request retains both independently declared routes.

requirements.title: Operative clarity has priority
requirements.statement: Operative text must state the exact action, state, consequence, scope, or recovery without relying on imagery, implication, color, sound, or spatial inference.
conflicts: Atmosphere obscuring action or trust-boundary meaning

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Operative outputs remain immediately understandable when read without surrounding visual context.

tests.assertion: Actions and model boundaries are stated directly.
An implication-only instruction is prohibited.
Interpretive companion text cannot weaken the paired operative statement.

requirements.title: Evidence-bounded learning
requirements.statement: Turn and outcome learning copy must distinguish recorded diagnostic evidence, committed matrix failure, absence of a tracked finding, and absence of causal proof; score alone must not manufacture blame or exoneration.
conflicts: No clear mistake claims based on incomplete diagnostics
Strongest-cause ranking without a ranking rule

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Learning text names only tracked mismatches, findings, matrix results, and limits supported by the record.

tests.assertion: A typed mismatch produces the corresponding bounded adjustment copy.
A low score without a tracked finding does not produce a causal mistake claim.
Committed matrix failure and no tracked finding can be stated together without implying full compliance.

requirements.title: Accessibility equivalence is preserved
requirements.statement: Lattice adoption must not remove, contradict, or replace semantic names, state descriptions, recovery instructions, or nonvisual equivalents; automated checks do not establish human accessibility approval.
conflicts: Meaning available only through figurative, visual, spatial, or tonal inference

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Adopted copy preserves the same operational meaning in semantic DOM and text-only use.

tests.assertion: Accessible names and descriptions retain required state and consequence.
Copy dependent on color, sound, or placement is rejected.
Automated coverage is reported separately from unperformed assistive-technology testing.

requirements.title: Presentation copy cannot decide mechanics
requirements.statement: Adopted Lattice output must be downstream of typed game state and diagnostic codes and must never be parsed to determine scoring, contact disclosure, catalog credit, scenario validity, or adjudication.
conflicts: Regular expressions or substring checks over player-facing prose controlling state

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Changing adopted presentation text cannot change any game-state result.

tests.assertion: Typed diagnostic codes select learning copy.
Prose-regex classification in the adopted learning path is prohibited.
Unresolved prose-to-logic couplings outside the slice keep broad adoption blocked.

requirements.title: Runtime payload is text-only
requirements.statement: The browser runtime may receive only the compact generated text map and its four-field release envelope; it may not contain the Lattice engine, profile, requests, atoms, assertions, receipts, source catalog, or review metadata.
conflicts: Shipping owner-only Lattice material to the browser

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Built assets contain all 26 selected strings and none of the owner-only Lattice materials.

tests.assertion: The runtime payload has exactly the allowed envelope and text map.
Owner request IDs, digests, receipts, atoms, or traceability fields in any textual asset fail validation.
Non-JavaScript textual assets are scanned as well as bundles.

requirements.title: Owner evidence is content-addressed and separate
requirements.statement: Owner-side generated output, evidence snapshot, and index must bind the pinned inputs, implementation authorities, requests, outputs, assertion results, and traceability digest without relying on runtime artifacts to validate themselves. Identical compilation bytes are a no-op; changed files are replaced individually without a cross-file transaction claim.
conflicts: Generated output serving as its own authority

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Independent verification recomputes every bound digest from declared inputs.

tests.assertion: A current snapshot verifies from its pinned owner inputs.
Mutation of generated or evidence content is detected.
An unchanged content-addressed snapshot is not rewritten as new evidence.

requirements.title: Bidirectional requirement and inventory traceability
requirements.statement: Each request must reference existing active FOS-LAT semantic requirement IDs and FOS-COPY inventory IDs, and every adopted inventory target must be owned by the expected request and generated output.
conflicts: Dangling, duplicated, exempt, or superseded traceability references

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Traceability closes in both request-to-register and inventory-to-request directions.

tests.assertion: All 19 requests resolve their requirement, inventory, and source references.
An unknown or exempt adopted reference fails.
Shared route inventory units accept only their declared request set.

requirements.title: Provided-candidate identity
requirements.statement: Every output marked as provided must equal the exact text of its selected declared candidate, identified by candidate ID, layer, and representation.
conflicts: Receipt-valid substituted prose

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Candidate identity is checked before operative-content assertions and again offline.

tests.assertion: Every provided output matches its candidate byte-for-byte.
Substituting any of the 26 texts while retaining metadata fails.
A literal fallback is governed by its distinct source type rather than treated as provided.

requirements.title: No human-review claim
requirements.statement: Every request review record must state humanStatus not-claimed, and product documentation must not describe the Lattice copy as human-, accessibility-, or domain-approved.
conflicts: Approved, reviewed, certified, or validated language without corresponding human evidence

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Human review is consistently recorded as not claimed.

tests.assertion: All 19 request review objects carry humanStatus not-claimed.
Changing any review status to approved fails.
Automated checks are described as automated evidence, not human review.

requirements.title: Academy curriculum lint is advisory
requirements.statement: Academy curriculum-data lint may report required and prohibited patterns in bounded batches but may not rewrite lessons, quizzes, citations, or answers or claim comprehensive educational review.
conflicts: Automated lint represented as full Academy adoption or sourcing

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Lint is read-only, advisory, and limited to Academy curriculum data.

tests.assertion: The corpus is enumerated deterministically in bounded batches.
Lint cannot modify academyData or mark it approved.
Selected Academy chrome copy remains separate from curriculum-data lint.

requirements.title: Broad adoption remains blocked
requirements.statement: Product-wide Lattice transformation must remain blocked until prose-to-logic couplings in gameModel.ts, catalogMath.ts, and contactVisualization.ts are replaced by typed state and separately verified.
conflicts: Claiming product-wide adoption from the bounded slice

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: All three couplings remain explicit blockers until code and tests prove their removal.

tests.assertion: The inventory names each blocker and excludes it from adoption.
Changing broad status to adopted while a coupling remains fails.
Completing one coupling does not clear the other two.

requirements.title: Owner material is absent from release artifacts
requirements.statement: No request, candidate, atom, receipt, source catalog, traceability, review, profile, engine, or owner-package material may be emitted in any release textual asset.
conflicts: Development evidence bundled as public runtime data

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Every non-binary emitted file is scanned for owner-only markers.

tests.assertion: A normal build contains only the allowed text map.
Injecting owner metadata into JSON, text, HTML, or JavaScript fails.
Known binary assets are explicitly allowlisted rather than decoded as text.

requirements.title: Replay regenerates presentation copy
requirements.statement: Save import and canonical replay must validate adjudication fields and regenerate Lattice presentation prose from typed state rather than trusting serialized display strings.
conflicts: Persisted prose becoming adjudication authority

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Display prose can change between builds without changing or invalidating a mechanically identical canonical replay.

tests.assertion: A canonical save replays and regenerates current presentation prose.
Altered adjudication fields remain rejected even with plausible prose.
Legacy non-authoritative history remains bounded without becoming current rule evidence.

requirements.title: Unscored-writing claim is exact
requirements.statement: Outcome copy must state that written responses were not evaluated and must attribute the result to the model's invented rules, recorded game state, and selected orders without claiming numeric rules are the only inputs.
conflicts: Only numeric rules and selected orders determined the result

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: The unscored-writing note preserves both non-evaluation and the full bounded input attribution.

tests.assertion: The exact non-evaluation claim appears in outcomes.
The old numeric-rules-only overclaim is prohibited.
Exporting player writing does not imply that adjudication reads it.

requirements.title: Scenario validation claims are bounded
requirements.statement: Copy may claim validation of the implemented structured coexistence checks but may not call a scenario fully feasible, completely validated, winnable, nontrivial, doctrinally sound, or politically coherent without separate evidence.
conflicts: Structured coexistence represented as complete feasibility

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Player and design copy names the bounded structured checks and their unresolved semantic limits.

tests.assertion: Coexistence validation is described accurately.
Fully validated or impossible-combinations language is absent from current claims.
Historical red-team evidence remains unaltered and explicitly historical.

requirements.title: Field Guide bounded adoption
requirements.statement: Seven Field Guide subjects must consume paired operative and interpretive outputs routed across technical, action, analysis, public-notice, and aftermath registers while retaining exact mechanics in the operative layer.
conflicts: Calling the Field Guide a complete scoring specification

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: missionCredit, scenarioAcceptance, uncrewedUndersea, commandTurns, strategicFit, modelBoundary, and missionLearning each render two generated layers.

tests.assertion: All fourteen Field Guide output targets are used.
Hard-coded duplicate prose for an adopted section is rejected.
Catalog tables and exact pairings remain outside the interpretive rewrite.

requirements.title: Academy selected-surface adoption
requirements.statement: Lattice output may replace only the Academy compare introduction, sources introduction, model boundary, independence status, and language-system explanation in this slice.
conflicts: Representing the full Academy curriculum as transformed or reviewed

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Exactly five selected Academy chrome outputs are consumed and curriculum content remains unchanged by compilation.

tests.assertion: All five exact Academy keys render from generated copy.
No request owns a lesson answer or citation claim.
Compare user notes remain user-authored and untransformed.

requirements.title: Debrief selected-surface adoption
requirements.statement: Seven turn and outcome learning outputs must be routed through the three independent debrief units: consequential after-action interpretation, ambient pending status, and technical report copy.
conflicts: One route shared across pending, report, and after-action meanings

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: The seven exact learning keys are generated and selected by typed state.

tests.assertion: Every supported learning state resolves a generated heading and summary.
Unknown or prose-inferred state cannot select a learning message.
No-final-finding fallback avoids both blame and success claims.

requirements.title: Hashed source-symbol identity
requirements.statement: The request source catalog must identify exactly 12 TypeScript declarations by contained repository path, declaration kind and name, and source digest; a digest proves identity only, not truth or approval.
conflicts: Path-only provenance
Hash represented as semantic validation

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: All referenced declarations exist in TypeScript AST and match their declared digests.

tests.assertion: Exactly 12 catalog symbols resolve and hash correctly.
Path escape, symlink escape, missing declaration, or hash drift fails.
Two declarations in one file remain separately identified while sharing file containment.

requirements.title: Closed governance schemas
requirements.statement: The requirement register, copy inventory, authoring request, generated owner output, runtime output, evidence snapshot, and evidence index must use versioned closed schemas that reject unknown fields.
conflicts: Permissive metadata that bypasses verification

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Every governed object has additionalProperties false or an equivalent exact-key check.

tests.assertion: Canonical governance and output documents validate.
Representative undeclared fields at owner and runtime object levels fail.
Runtime v1 remains its explicitly bounded four-field schema while owner documents use v2.

requirements.title: Browser evidence is not overstated
requirements.statement: Listing or compiling browser tests must not be described as executing browser assertions; documentation must state when compatible Chromium is unavailable.
conflicts: Browser inventory represented as live browser execution

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Static/browser inventory evidence and executed-browser evidence remain separate.

tests.assertion: Documentation labels the browser suite as listed when not executed.
A passed-browser claim without an executed result is prohibited.
Unit and build success may be reported independently of browser execution.

requirements.title: Academy sourcing remains bounded
requirements.statement: Selected Academy interface copy and curriculum-data lint must not be represented as a complete review of lesson accuracy, source coverage, citation quality, quiz validity, or learner comprehension.
conflicts: Full Academy sourcing or educational validation claim

acceptanceCriteria.assertion: Current documentation identifies the selected UI copy and advisory lint scope and names unverified educational questions.

tests.assertion: The Academy scope statement is bounded to five outputs and advisory curriculum-data lint.
Comprehensive, approved, or fully sourced Academy language is prohibited.
Existing reading lists may be described without claiming the lint authenticated them.
